passage:
A museum had an old printing press that visitors could try. Students placed metal letters in a frame, added ink, and pressed paper onto them.
It took several minutes to print one page. Students thought about how quickly modern printers work.
The guide explained that printing technology once changed the spread of knowledge. Books became easier to produce, and ideas could travel faster.
After using the press, students respected old books more. Each page had required labor.
The printing press showed that information revolutions existed before the internet. Every age has tools that change who can read, learn, and speak.
